01-six-screens.svg.title: Information from screen and sound
01-six-screens.svg.desc: A recovery code tutorial video wireframe with six scenes arranged in two columns and three rows in reading order. Screen information and original audio information are shown separately for each scene. The security check failure scene has a failure message and a retry button, but the original audio contains only two warning beeps. The new code scene contains the fictional training code R7K2-P9M4, and the final scene shows that saving is complete and the previous code is unusable.
labels: Reading order: left → right, top → bottom · Observed intervals rounded
Do not discard the old code
Guidance to save safely. Old code
Recorded fictional demo · No real account operations · Compare screen and sound information separately.

02-decision-branches.svg.title: 1.2.3 options and decision flow
02-decision-branches.svg.desc: The evaluation flow for 1.2.3. After checking applicability and the exception for a media alternative for text, review whether the original audio conveys all important visual information. If additional description is needed, check audio description and alternatives for time-based media. The criterion is met if one sufficient method is verified across the full scope. If only a defect in one method is confirmed and the status of other methods is unclear, the judgment is deferred. A judgment of not met requires confirmation that no other sufficient method exists.
labels: Check scope of applicability and original evidence
Check both conditions for the text-alternative exception
No information beyond the text + clearly labeled as a media alternative
Does original audio convey all key screen information?
If so, additional audio description is not needed
in text in the same order
One sufficient method verified across full scope → Met
One candidate defective + other methods unverified → Deferred
All methods checked + no sufficient method → Not met
Insufficient original evidence → Deferred, even if candidate is detailed
Distinguish a single candidate's defect from failure of the entire criterion.
Evaluate the audio description requirement of 1.2.5 (AA) separately.

04-scene-to-alternative.svg.title: Linking the original to an alternative
04-scene-to-alternative.svg.desc: Links screen and audio information from the failure, new code, and completion scenes to paragraphs 3, 5, and 6 of the alternative. Preserves the failure message and warning beeps, the fictional code value and saving guidance, and the specific completion results together. The final review items cover meaning, negation, order, and access paths.
labels: Linking the original to an alternative
First identify information units in the original, then compare candidate paragraphs.
Guidance to save in a safe place
Keep value, action, dialogue in paragraph 5
Saved + old code no longer usable
□ Missing meaning  □ Reversed negation  □ Order  □ Actual access path
Scene numbers and timecodes are not required formats.
Demo screen buttons ≠ actual viewer input
If interaction actually exists, check equivalent means for choices and results.

03-coverage-matrix.svg.title: Transcript versus full alternative
03-coverage-matrix.svg.desc: Compares a transcript and a full alternative for the failure scene. The transcript of dialogue and sounds contains only two warning beeps. The alternative enhanced with visual description includes the security check failure message, retry button, and warning beeps. Audio description conveys visual information through sound alongside the original audio, while a media alternative conveys screens, dialogue, and sounds in text in the same order.
labels: Compare directly what is missing from the same failure scene.
Adding visual information to a transcript can yield a sufficient media alternative.
Original audio + needed visual description → understood through sound. No duty to retranscribe original audio.
Screen + dialogue + meaningful sounds → understood through text in the same order.
Check actual content and access paths, not just the format's name.
Audio description can also convey all necessary visual information.
If dialogue is dense, consider extended description or description-integrated narration.

This material provides the same information in the same order as the recovery code issuance guide video. These are fictional training screens that cannot be used with real accounts.
1. The security settings screen shows the ‘Settings → Security → Recovery codes’ path and the ‘Issue new code’ button. The guide says, “Select Security in Settings.” The user asks, “Can I discard the old code now?”
2. The ‘Before issuance’ screen displays a Keep old code button and the warning “Do not discard the old code before saving the new code.” The guide replies, “No. Do not discard it before saving the new recovery code.”
3. The security check failure screen displays the message “Security check failed. Please authenticate again.” and the ‘Retry security check’ button. Two warning beeps signal the security check failure.
4. The reauthentication complete screen displays the message “Security check complete. Confirm new code issuance.” and the ‘Confirm issuance’ button. The guide says, “After repeating the security check, confirm issuance.”
5. The new recovery code screen shows the fictional training code R7K2-P9M4, the notice “The code on this screen cannot be used with real accounts.” and the ‘Save code’ button. The guide says, “Save the new code in a safe place. Once a new code is issued, the old code can no longer be used.”
6. The issuance complete screen displays “New code saved · Old code no longer usable” and the ‘Return to settings’ button. The guide says, “Check the issuance complete screen.”
The buttons in the video are part of the demonstration screens; no actual button presses are performed. The page's video player provides playback, pause, and seeking.
